reviews.review_text:

Delicious meal, good (maybe a little too attentive) service! Come during 5-7:30 happy hour!
Jan 2020
After months in Asia, I was really craving some good Mexican. I've tried a few places in Hanoi and Da Nang, but this one was the first that was really really good! The food came out very fast.

The lovely waitress informed me I was in during the happy hour (50% off selected drinks that have a skull symbol on the menu), so I ordered myself a Mexican Mule, which was a tequila take on one of my favorite cocktails- very refreshing, though not served in the classic mule mug. But then, this was a Mexican mule, not a Moscow mule, so no minus points there!

The Pollo Tostada was delicious...mmmm fresh queso! The carnitas taco, also amazingly flavorful meat. I don't normally eat pork, but I had a feeling about this taco, and boy was I right!

I didn't love the Baja fish taco- the breading on the fish was a bit too thick and greasy for my liking. I like a very crispy and lightly coated fish. Also, the filling was too much for the taco (not something to really complain about, I know) so it's a bit hard to eat because of the two bulky pieces of fish. One suggestion that a mexican restaurant back home does is provide a double layer of tortilla under the filling so the diner can portion it out (so still the same amt of filling) but with a bit more tortilla for it.

When I ordered, the waitress asked me if I was ok with spicy food (that's how you definitely know you are not in Mexico!). I said yes, spicy is great. But later I was confused, because I did not feel any of the food was even the slightest bit spicy. I mean, the place IS named Gringo so I guess they cater to a gringo level of spice tolerance, which is too little for the rest of us! 

I finished off my meal with an order of churros, because why not treat yoself. They were a bit over done, but still tasty. I prefer them without the chocolate dipping sauce. I ate the churros first and then the chocolate after, as the chocolate dampens the taste and texture of the sugar coating that is so nice.

Overall, an unexpectedly excellent meal that all together cost about $15. A bit pricy for the backpacker crowd, but in my opinion very reasonable for the quality of the food and given that it included an alcoholic drink, main course, and dessert.

The only other thing that took away a bit from the dining experience is that one of the staff (a new male waiter) was apparently trying to get his 1000 steps in for the day, pacing back and forth constantly between the bar and the front door. I swear he went back and forth more than 40 times while I was sitting there. I agree that attentive service is great, but there is definitely a line between attentive and hovering. I mean, I was a bit self conscious while trying to have a romantic moment with my carnitas taco, and it's very distracting to have someone passing by your table and looking at you too much. Some privacy please! I'm sure it's just because he's new and eager to be on top of things, and maybe if I wasn't dining solo it wouldn't have been so annoying because I'd be distracted by conversation.

So, just a friendly suggestion to maybe let him know to tone it down a bit, or if he wants to hover, maybe do it from afar rather than pacing back and forth constantly. However, he was extremely lovely and friendly otherwise, as were all the more relaxed female staff.

Hello GaryWW_11,

Thanks for visiting us and leaving a review. I’m sorry you were disappointed with your experience here.
Our homemade corn tortilla chips are made with maseca (corn flour) that we import from California, not flour as you stated. I do apologize if they were hard. That happens if they are left to fry for too long. Based on your description of the salsa I’m guessing that you ordered the “ranchero salsa” (mild). There is no catsup (or ketchup), mayonnaise or cayenne used in our ranchero salsa (or in anything on our menu). We make the ranchero salsa fresh in house using only fresh produce that includes tomatoes, onion, garlic, chilis, oregano, pork lard and salt. It’s the same salsa that is commonly found served with “huevos rancheros” and we then blend it which gives it the creamy texture that you mistook for mayonnaise. 

The burrito that you’re describing sounds like our “carnitas” (slow cooked pork). We slow cook pork shoulder in pork lard and other seasonings for 6 hours. You are correct, we do cook our carnitas with cinnamon and the sweet that you’re tasting is condensed milk that is included to help keep the pork moist. However, the sweetness is not overpowering. It’s a family recipe from one of my former cooks in America who was born in and grew up in Mexico. Vietnam is full of wonderful local food, but any traveler gets homesick for some comfort food sooner or later. Nothing fits squarely into my comfort zone more snugly than some good street tacos with a decent craft beer. Now, good street tacos were the last thing I expected to see in Ho Chi Minh City, but like so many other things in this wonderful city, you never know what's around the next corner.

Gringo's is very conveniently located in District One, not far from the main Bien Thuy market, backpacker street, and downtown museums. The owner, Doug, is a SoCal transplant that embodies the old adage, "necessity is the mother of invention", and when he found himself with an incurable itch for a good taco, he rolled up his sleeves and starting making them. Starting out with a cart in the seafood market, he moved to a more traditional spot a few years ago, and the rest is history.

I happened to be in Gringos at the same time a young lady from Mexico was visiting, and she was highly complimentary of her meal. My fish tacos were exceptional- and the locally brewed craft been I washed it down with hit the comfort spot as well (most local beers in SE Asia tend to be light pilsner-types).

When you find yourself in HCMC jonzing for some comfort food- or just a great meal, stop in and shoot the breeze with Doug while enjoying a beer and some great tacos!

The mole rojo (red) sauce that it is topped with is made from dried ancho and pasilla chilis that turn from red to a dark brown color when dried. Also as part of this drying process the chilis take on a naturally slightly bitter flavor. I went to Gringos on the recommendation of a colleague, and have now been two days in a row with plans to return tomorrow. Gringo Tacos is relatively new, opening a few months ago, and the place is spotless, well laid out, and has a friendly and inviting atmosphere. The menu, while simple, offers lots of choices. I've tried all their soft tacos, and their Quesadillas, and plan to sample burritos and more. Everything - and I mean everything (almost) - is made on site, fresh, and canned or frozen doesn't cut it. The taco shells (gluten free, even!) are made on site, and taste it! 

Standouts for me (after two visits with many more planned) are the spicy salsa (which has real taste to it without being overly hot and spicy) and the pulled pork, which is sublime. The owner of the restaurant, a transplanted chef from LA, puts his heart into everything, and is always checking in with customers to make sure they are content. The margaritas are good, too, and make a fine cap to a wonderful meal. All this at a really fair price, too!

Gringo Tacos will be one of my go-to destinations a few times a week when I'm in Saigon (which is often). The food really is that good! Stand-out Mexican cuisine in Saigon...who'd a thunk it?
